newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt paper yields mostly lower in active trade.
newsitem.headline: HK govt paper yields mostly lower in active trade.

text.p: Interbank rates fell and government paper yields tended lower on Thursday in active trading on a continued inflow of regional funds, dealers said.
Overnight cash eased to 4-5/8 9/16 percent from 4-13/16 11/16 at midday Wednesday, and three-month money was 5-3/8 5/16 versus 5-7/16 5/16 percent.
Short-term money continued to enjoy high liquidity as funds were seen flowing into the market as Hong Kong's political uncertainties were gradually eased, one dealer said.
A major lender was seen offering one-month and longer-dated money in the market, another dealer added.
Dealers noted active trading on Exchange Fund bills and notes with interest focused on short-dated issues.
One-week Exchange Fund bills yields fell to 3.83 percent from 4.13 percent.
The yield for three-year notes was 6.14 versus 6.16, five-year note yields were 6.58 versus 6.59, seven-year note was 6.79 versus 6.81.
But 10-year note yield edged up to 7.02 from 7.00 percent.
Dealers expected Exchange Fund Bill yields to fall on Friday on anticipation of "satisfactory" auction results of five-year U.S. Treasury notes due later in the day.
